## Purpose and Public Entry Points
This is a Python RLM library: it wraps API/local language models in a recursive execution harness, allowing a root model to inspect offloaded context in a Python REPL and invoke LM or nested RLM calls. Public imports originate at `rlm/__init__.py`; the principal orchestration API is `rlm/core/rlm.py`. Examples such as `examples/quickstart.py` and `examples/rlm_query_batched_example.py` demonstrate application integration.

## RLM Orchestrator and Completion Lifecycle
`RLM` constructs a model backend plus execution environment, then drives `completion()` iterations. It supplies the prompt/context/history to the environment, accepts generated code, executes it, feeds observations back to the root LM, and terminates with an `RLMChatCompletion`-style result and optional trajectory metadata.
- `rlm/core/rlm.py`
- `rlm/core/types.py`
- `rlm/core/lm_handler.py`

## LM Abstraction and Recursive Dispatch
The LM handler mediates root and subcalls, including batched calls and concurrency/depth constraints. REPL-visible functions such as single/batched LM queries and recursive RLM queries route from generated code back through host-side orchestration, a necessary boundary for isolated environments. Provider adapters normalize provider-specific API behavior behind the base interface.
- `rlm/core/comms_utils.py`
- `rlm/clients/base_lm.py`
- `rlm/clients/openai.py`

Supported external model services include OpenAI/Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Portkey/OpenRouter-style routing; local vLLM is accessed through the OpenAI-compatible client.
- `rlm/clients/anthropic.py`
- `rlm/clients/gemini.py`
- `rlm/clients/portkey.py`

## REPL Execution and Isolation Boundary
Environment implementations execute model-authored Python against context and tools. `LocalREPL` is the default same-process `exec` environment; IPython can run in process or a kernel subprocess. Persistent sessions retain versioned context/history between completions, while compaction summarizes running history. This is the main trust boundary: local execution shares host dependencies and is unsuitable for untrusted production inputs.
- `rlm/environments/base_env.py`
- `rlm/environments/local_repl.py`
- `rlm/environments/ipython_repl.py`

Container/cloud implementations isolate code but proxy recursive LM requests to the host. Docker requires a Docker runtime; Modal, Prime, Daytona, and E2B rely on their corresponding sandbox services/SDKs.
- `rlm/environments/docker_repl.py`
- `rlm/environments/modal_repl.py`
- `rlm/environments/prime_repl.py`

## Prompts, Parsing, and Execution Contracts
Core utility modules define system prompts, parse model outputs into executable actions/results, count or manage tokens, and centralize domain exceptions. These form the contract between model text generation, REPL execution, and the iterative controller.
- `rlm/utils/prompts.py`
- `rlm/utils/parsing.py`
- `rlm/utils/token_utils.py`

## Observability and Trajectory Visualization
The logger records configuration, root iterations, code execution, and nested calls as in-memory metadata and optionally JSONL files. A separate Next.js visualizer ingests these logs client-side and presents execution, trajectory, iteration, and aggregate views.
- `rlm/logger/rlm_logger.py`
- `visualizer/src/lib/parse-logs.ts`
- `visualizer/src/components/Dashboard.tsx`

## Training Subproject
`training/` is an intentionally separate Python package integrating RLM execution with `verifiers` and Prime Intellect `prime-rl`. It exposes an RLM-backed task environment, uses subprocess-isolated local REPL execution, and defines workers, proxying, scoring rubrics, and configurable training jobs. OOLONG is the worked long-context QA environment.
- `training/src/rlm_train/env.py`
- `training/src/rlm_train/worker.py`
- `training/environments/oolong/oolong/env.py`

## Documentation and Delivery
The distributable Python package is defined by `pyproject.toml` and targets Python 3.11+. Documentation is a separate Next.js site, while GitHub Actions publish the package and deploy/check docs. The docs and visualizer are supporting Node.js applications, not runtime dependencies of inference.
- `pyproject.toml`
- `docs/src/app/page.tsx`
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`
